title: Design a Dark Mode Toggle
description: A popular web app needs a smooth dark mode feature that remembers the user's preference across sessions.
task: Design and describe how you would build a dark mode toggle for a React app. Consider: where to store the preference, how to apply it globally, and how to make the transition smooth.
hint: Think about localStorage for persistence, CSS variables for theming, and a Context API for sharing the state.
approach: Use React Context + useState to hold the theme. Save it to localStorage on change so it persists. Apply a 'dark' class to the root element and use CSS variables like --bg-color and --text-color that change based on the class. Add a smooth CSS transition: transition: background 0.3s, color 0.3s. On app load, read from localStorage to set initial theme.

title: Build a Typing Speed Tracker
description: A student wants a simple web tool to measure how fast they type in words per minute.
task: Describe how you would build a typing speed test app. What components would you need? How would you calculate WPM? How would you show the result to the user?
hint: WPM = (total characters typed / 5) / minutes elapsed. Start the timer on first keypress.
approach: Show a random paragraph to type. Start a timer when the user begins typing. Compare each character typed against the target text. On completion calculate WPM = (chars / 5) / (elapsed seconds / 60). Show accuracy as (correct chars / total chars) * 100. Use useState for the timer, typed text, and results. Highlight correct letters in green and mistakes in red in real time.

title: Create a Meme Generator
description: Users want to upload an image and add custom top and bottom text to create a meme in seconds.
task: Plan and describe how you would build a meme generator app. How would you let users upload images, add text overlay, and download the final meme?
hint: HTML Canvas can draw images and text together, then export as a downloadable image file.
approach: Use an HTML file input for image upload and FileReader to load it. Draw on a Canvas element: first drawImage() then fillText() for top and bottom captions with white text and black stroke for contrast. Let users type text in input fields and update the canvas in real time. For download, use canvas.toDataURL() and create a temporary anchor tag with download attribute. Bonus: add font size and color pickers.

title: Design a Habit Tracker App
description: Someone wants to track their daily habits and see a streak of how many days in a row they completed each one.
task: Describe the data structure and UI design for a habit tracker app. How would you track streaks? How would you store data locally?
hint: Store habits as an array of objects, each with a name and an array of completed dates. Calculate streak by checking consecutive days backward from today.
approach: Data model: [{ id, name, completedDates: ['2025-01-01', ...] }]. Store in localStorage. UI: list of habit cards each with a checkbox for today and a streak count. To calculate streak: start from today, go backward day by day, count how many consecutive days appear in completedDates. Display a calendar heatmap for each habit using a CSS grid colored by completion. Add/remove habits via a simple form.

title: Build a Budget Splitter
description: A group of friends went on a trip and need to fairly split shared expenses — some paid more than others.
task: Design a bill splitting app where users can enter their names, list shared expenses (with who paid), and see who owes whom how much to settle up fairly.
hint: Calculate each person's total paid and their fair share. Anyone who paid less than fair share owes money, anyone who paid more is owed money.
approach: State: people array and expenses array [{description, amount, paidBy}]. Calculate total spent and fair share per person (total / numPeople). For each person: balance = totalPaid - fairShare. Positive balance = they are owed money, negative = they owe. Settle by matching biggest debtor with biggest creditor repeatedly until all balanced. Display a clear list: 'Alice pays Bob ₹500'. This greedy settlement approach minimizes the number of transactions.

title: Design an Offline-First Notes App
description: A productivity app should let users write and access their notes even with no internet connection.
task: Explain how you would architect a notes app that works offline, syncs when connection returns, and handles conflicts if the same note was edited in two places.
hint: Service Workers enable offline caching. IndexedDB stores structured data locally. Think about what happens when you edit offline and then come online.
approach: Use a Service Worker to cache the app shell and API responses. Store notes in IndexedDB locally for instant reads/writes. When online, sync with backend using a queue of pending changes stored locally. For conflict resolution: use timestamps — last-write-wins for simple cases, or flag the conflict and show both versions for user to choose. Use the Background Sync API to retry failed sync when connection returns. Show a subtle 'offline' badge in the UI so users know their state.

title: Gamify a Learning Dashboard
description: An e-learning platform wants to add game mechanics to motivate students to complete more lessons.
task: Design a gamification system for a learning platform. What game elements would you add? How would you implement XP, badges, streaks, and leaderboards without making it feel forced?
hint: The best gamification is invisible — it should feel like natural progress, not a game bolted on top. Focus on intrinsic motivation.
approach: XP System: award points for completing lessons, quizzes, helping others. Level up at milestones with a satisfying animation. Badges: specific achievements like '7-day streak', 'first quiz aced', 'helped 10 people'. Make them rare enough to feel earned. Streak: daily login + activity counter, show a flame icon, send gentle reminders. Leaderboard: weekly reset so new users can compete, show only top 10 + user's own rank to avoid discouraging those far behind. Progress bars for each course to show how close they are to completion.

title: Create an AI Recipe Suggester
description: A busy person wants to take photos of ingredients in their fridge and get recipe suggestions for what they can cook.
task: Design the system architecture for an app that identifies ingredients from a photo and suggests recipes. What AI models would you use? How would you handle the full user flow?
hint: You need two AI steps: first identify what's in the image, then use that list to find or generate recipes.
approach: Step 1: Use a vision AI model (like GPT-4 Vision or Google Vision API) to analyze the uploaded photo and return a list of identified ingredients. Step 2: Send that ingredient list to an LLM prompt like 'Suggest 3 recipes using mostly these ingredients: {list}. Include cooking time and difficulty.' Display recipe cards with title, ingredients needed, missing ingredients highlighted in red, and step-by-step instructions. Cache results so same ingredients don't re-query. Let users save favorite recipes to a local collection.

title: Design a Real-Time Collaborative Whiteboard
description: A remote team needs a shared digital whiteboard where multiple people can draw and add notes simultaneously.
task: Plan the architecture for a real-time collaborative whiteboard. How would you sync drawing actions between multiple users? How would you handle latency and conflicts?
hint: WebSockets enable real-time bidirectional communication. Think about what data to broadcast — the full canvas or just the drawing actions?
approach: Use WebSockets (via Socket.io) to broadcast drawing events in real-time. Each event contains: {userId, tool, startX, startY, endX, endY, color, width}. Never sync the full canvas — only sync actions and replay them on each client's local canvas. Use Operational Transformation or CRDT for conflict-free merging. Assign each user a unique color cursor. Store a history of all events so late joiners can replay from the start. For performance, batch multiple events per frame using requestAnimationFrame. Add undo/redo by reversing events in the local history.

title: Build a Smart Bookmark Manager
description: A developer bookmarks hundreds of links but can never find them later — they need intelligent organization and search.
task: Design a smart bookmark manager that automatically categorizes saved links and lets users search by content, not just title. How would you make search fast and intelligent?
hint: Auto-tagging can use the page's meta tags and Open Graph data. Full-text search of page content requires crawling and indexing the saved pages.
approach: When a URL is saved: fetch the page, extract title, description, Open Graph tags, and main text content. Use an LLM to generate 3-5 relevant tags automatically. Store everything in an indexed local database (IndexedDB or SQLite via WASM). For search: implement fuzzy search on title + description + tags using Fuse.js, and keyword search on full page content. Show preview cards with favicon, title, auto-tags, and a snippet of the page description. Group by auto-detected category (article, video, tool, docs). Add a browser extension so users can save with one click.

title: Design a Pomodoro Focus Timer
description: A developer wants a focus timer that helps them stay productive using the Pomodoro technique with customizable intervals.
task: Describe how you would build a Pomodoro timer app with work sessions, short breaks, and long breaks. How would you notify the user when a session ends?
hint: Use setInterval for the countdown and the Web Notifications API to alert the user even when the tab is in the background.
approach: State: mode ('work'|'shortBreak'|'longBreak'), timeLeft, sessionCount, isRunning. Durations: work=25min, shortBreak=5min, longBreak=15min. Use setInterval to tick timeLeft every second. When timeLeft reaches 0: auto-advance to next mode (after every 4 work sessions, trigger long break), play a sound, send a browser notification. Show a circular progress ring using SVG stroke-dashoffset. Let users customize durations. Persist session count in localStorage so progress survives page refreshes.

title: Build a Personal Finance Dashboard
description: A user wants to track their monthly income, expenses by category, and savings rate in one place.
task: Design a personal finance tracker with transaction input, category-based spending breakdown, and a savings rate indicator. How would you visualize the data?
hint: Use a pie or donut chart for category breakdown, a line chart for monthly trends, and a simple metric card for savings rate.
approach: Data model: transactions = [{id, date, amount, type:'income'|'expense', category, note}]. Group by category to compute totals. Savings rate = (income - expenses) / income * 100. Use Recharts or Chart.js for the donut chart. Store in localStorage. Add filters for date range (this month, last 3 months, all time). Color-code categories consistently. Show a running balance line chart over time. Export to CSV for spreadsheet use.

title: Create a Flashcard Learning App
description: A student wants a spaced repetition flashcard app to learn vocabulary more efficiently than re-reading notes.
task: Design a flashcard app with spaced repetition. How would you decide which cards to show next? How would you animate the card flip?
hint: The SM-2 algorithm is the classic spaced repetition algorithm — cards rated hard come back sooner, easy ones come back later.
approach: Card model: {id, front, back, easeFactor, interval, nextReview}. Show cards due today (nextReview <= today). After reviewing, user rates: Again(1), Hard(2), Good(3), Easy(4). Update interval using SM-2: new_interval = interval * ease_factor. Animate flip with CSS: transform: rotateY(180deg) on click, backface-visibility: hidden to show reverse. Group cards into decks. Show a daily review counter. Add progress charts showing learned vs due cards over time.

title: Design a Code Snippet Manager
description: A developer constantly copy-pastes useful code snippets from old projects but can never find them when needed.
task: Build a code snippet manager where developers can save, tag, search, and copy snippets with syntax highlighting. How would you make search fast and relevant?
hint: Use a code editor library like CodeMirror or Prism.js for syntax highlighting. Store snippets with tags for fast filtering.
approach: Snippet model: {id, title, code, language, tags[], createdAt, usageCount}. For syntax highlighting: use Prism.js with language auto-detection. Search: fuzzy match on title + tags using Fuse.js, full-text search on code content. Tag cloud sidebar for quick filtering. One-click copy to clipboard with visual confirmation. Sort by 'most recently used' or 'most copied' to surface relevant snippets. Export/import as JSON for backup. Add a VS Code extension integration for inserting directly into editor.

title: Build a URL Shortener
description: A team needs a private URL shortener to create clean links for their marketing campaigns and track click counts.
task: Design the backend and frontend for a URL shortener. How would you generate unique short codes? How would you handle redirects and track analytics?
hint: Generate short codes using base62 encoding of an auto-incremented ID. Store in a key-value database for O(1) lookup.
approach: Short code generation: take the auto-increment DB id, encode in base62 (0-9, a-z, A-Z) to get a 6-char code. Store: {shortCode, originalUrl, createdAt, clickCount, createdBy}. Redirect: GET /abc123 → lookup in Redis/DB → HTTP 301 redirect. Analytics: log each click with {ip, userAgent, referrer, timestamp}. Dashboard shows: total clicks, clicks over time chart, top referrers, geographic breakdown. Add custom aliases (e.g. /launch) for premium users. Rate limit creation to prevent abuse.

title: Design a Real-Time Chat Application
description: A startup needs an internal team chat app with channels, direct messages, and file sharing.
task: Design the architecture for a real-time chat application. How would you handle message delivery, online presence, and read receipts efficiently?
hint: WebSockets for real-time delivery, Redis pub/sub for horizontal scaling across multiple servers, and optimistic UI for instant feel.
approach: Frontend: WebSocket connection per user. Message send: optimistic UI (show immediately with 'sending' status), then confirm on server ACK. Presence: heartbeat every 30s, mark offline after 60s without heartbeat. Read receipts: batch them every 2s to avoid flooding. Backend: Node.js + Socket.io, Redis pub/sub to broadcast across multiple servers. Store messages in PostgreSQL, use Redis for active sessions and unread counts. Message model: {id, channelId, senderId, content, type, createdAt, editedAt, reactions}. Add push notifications for offline users via web-push.

title: Create a Weather Dashboard
description: A user wants a beautiful weather app that shows current conditions, a 7-day forecast, and hourly breakdown.
task: Design a weather dashboard that uses a public weather API. How would you handle location detection, unit conversion, and make the UI reflect current weather conditions?
hint: Use the Geolocation API for location, OpenWeatherMap free tier for data, and change background gradients/icons based on weather conditions.
approach: On load: request browser geolocation, or let user search by city. Fetch from OpenWeatherMap API (free tier). Display: large current temp, feels-like, humidity, wind speed. Horizontal scrollable hourly forecast for next 24 hours. 7-day forecast cards below. Dynamically change: background gradient (blue for clear, grey for cloudy, dark for night), animated weather icons. Toggle Celsius/Fahrenheit — store preference in localStorage. Show UV index, sunrise/sunset times. Cache API response for 30 minutes to avoid rate limiting.

title: Build a Kanban Task Board
description: A freelancer needs a visual Kanban board to manage client projects across columns like Todo, In Progress, and Done.
task: Design a drag-and-drop Kanban board. How would you implement smooth card dragging, column management, and persist state locally?
hint: Use the HTML5 Drag and Drop API or a library like @dnd-kit/core. Track card positions as ordered arrays in each column.
approach: Data model: {columns: [{id, title, cards: [{id, title, description, priority, dueDate}]}]}. Drag-and-drop: use @dnd-kit/sortable for smooth animations. On drag end: update state by moving card from source column array to target column array at the drop index. Persist full board state to localStorage on every change. Add card detail modal with description, labels, comments, and due date. Column creation/deletion. Card count badge per column. Keyboard accessibility for moving cards. Export board as JSON backup.

title: Design a Browser Extension
description: A reader wants a browser extension that saves articles to read later and estimates reading time.
task: Describe how you would build a 'Read Later' browser extension. How does it extract article content, estimate reading time, and sync across devices?
hint: Use the Readability.js library (same as Firefox's reader mode) to extract clean article content from any page.
approach: Manifest V3 extension. Popup shows current page title and a 'Save' button. On save: content script runs Readability.js to extract clean text, title, author, estimated read time (word count / 200 wpm). Store in extension storage (chrome.storage.sync for cross-device). Reading list popup: sorted by saved date, filter by unread/read. Open saved articles in a clean reader view that strips ads and navigation. Show progress bar when reading (scroll position). Daily reading streak tracker.

title: Build a Music Playlist Generator
description: A user wants to generate playlists based on mood, activity, or their listening history using a music API.
task: Design a mood-based playlist generator. How would you translate a mood input into audio features and find matching songs?
hint: Spotify's audio features API returns valence (happiness), energy, danceability, and tempo — combine these to match moods.
approach: Mood mapping: create a table mapping moods to audio feature ranges. E.g., 'happy' = high valence (0.7-1.0) + high energy (0.6-1.0). Use Spotify API to search tracks matching those feature ranges. Let user input mood in natural language → LLM converts to feature parameters. Show playlist with track names, artists, and preview buttons. Add 'more like this' and 'less like this' buttons to refine the playlist. Export to Spotify as a new playlist with one click.

title: Create a Portfolio Generator
description: A developer wants to create a personal portfolio website from a simple JSON config without writing HTML or CSS.
task: Design a portfolio generator that takes a JSON config (name, bio, skills, projects, social links) and renders a beautiful one-page portfolio. How would you let users customize the theme?
hint: Use a template system with CSS custom properties for theming. Let users choose from preset color schemes and section layouts.
approach: Config schema: {name, bio, avatar, skills[], projects:[{title, description, url, tags[]}], experience[], social:{github, linkedin}}. Render each section as a component. Theme system: offer 5 preset color schemes using CSS custom properties (--primary, --bg, --text). Live preview as user edits JSON config. Generate static HTML file for download. Add section visibility toggles. Animation on scroll using Intersection Observer. Responsive design with mobile-first approach. One-click deploy to GitHub Pages.

title: Design a Code Review Assistant
description: A team wants an AI tool that automatically reviews pull requests and flags common issues before human review.
task: Design an AI-powered code review system. What issues would you check for? How would you integrate with GitHub? How would you make the AI feedback specific and actionable?
hint: Use the GitHub API to read PR diffs. Send code chunks to an LLM with a structured prompt for specific feedback categories.
approach: GitHub App: webhook on PR open/update. Fetch the diff using GitHub API. Split diff into chunks by file. For each chunk, prompt LLM: 'Review this code change. Check for: (1) bugs/logic errors, (2) security vulnerabilities, (3) performance issues, (4) code style. Be specific and give line numbers.' Post inline comments via GitHub API. Add a summary comment with overall assessment. Track false positive rate by monitoring if developers dismiss or accept comments. Let teams configure which rule categories to enable.

title: Build a Language Learning App
description: A person wants to learn a new language through daily vocabulary practice with pronunciation feedback.
task: Design a language learning app with vocabulary flashcards, pronunciation practice, and conversational AI exercises. How would you implement speech recognition and feedback?
hint: Use the Web Speech API for speech recognition and text-to-speech. Use an LLM for conversational practice and feedback.
approach: Vocabulary: spaced repetition flashcards with audio pronunciation (text-to-speech). Pronunciation practice: user speaks word, Web Speech API transcribes, compare with expected. LLM rates pronunciation on a scale and shows common mistakes. Conversation mode: LLM acts as a native speaker in a scenario (cafe, job interview), user speaks responses. After each session: vocabulary quiz from words encountered, grammar points highlighted. Track: words learned, daily streak, pronunciation accuracy trend. Add phonetic guides (IPA) for difficult words.

title: Design a Job Application Tracker
description: A job seeker wants to track all their applications, interview stages, contacts, and follow-up reminders in one place.
task: Design a job application tracker with a Kanban-style pipeline. How would you remind users to follow up? How would you show statistics on their success rate?
hint: Use a pipeline with stages: Applied, Phone Screen, Technical, Offer, Rejected. Calculate days since last activity to trigger follow-up alerts.
approach: Pipeline stages: Wishlist → Applied → Phone Screen → Technical Round → Final Round → Offer → Accepted/Rejected. Card model: {company, role, appliedDate, contacts[], notes[], stage, salaryRange, jobUrl}. Dashboard stats: total applications, response rate, offer conversion rate, average days per stage. Follow-up reminder: if a card has been in 'Applied' for >7 days with no update, highlight it in yellow. Email follow-up template generator. Export all applications to CSV. Interview question bank linked to each company.

title: Create a Markdown Editor with Preview
description: A blogger wants a split-screen markdown editor that shows a live rendered preview as they type.
task: Describe how you would build a split-screen markdown editor. How would you synchronize scroll position between the editor and preview panels?
hint: Use a markdown parsing library like marked.js or remark. Sync scroll by calculating the percentage scrolled in one panel.
approach: Two-panel layout: left is a textarea (or CodeMirror editor), right is a div rendering HTML. Use marked.js to convert markdown to HTML on every keystroke (debounced 100ms). Scroll sync: calculate scrollPercentage = scrollTop / (scrollHeight - clientHeight) in one panel and apply same percentage to other panel. Toolbar buttons for bold, italic, headers, code blocks that insert markdown syntax. Auto-save to localStorage every 5 seconds. Export to HTML or PDF. Dark/light theme toggle. Word count and reading time in the status bar.

title: Build a Meeting Cost Calculator
description: A manager wants to know the real financial cost of meetings to help justify whether they're worth having.
task: Design a meeting cost calculator that shows the running dollar cost of a meeting based on attendees and their hourly rates. How would you make this impactful visually?
hint: Display a ticker that counts up every second. The psychological impact of seeing money tick away in real-time is the whole point.
approach: Input: list of attendees with optional salary estimates, or just number of people with average salary. Calculate: hourly cost = (annual salary / 52 / 40) * number of people. Start a timer that ticks every 100ms and updates the cost display. Show: large running total counter with dollar sign, cost per minute beside it, projected cost if meeting runs 30/60/90 minutes. Add optional 'Cost per insight' metric — total cost / number of action items. Export meeting summary. Sound of a cash register on start for effect.

title: Design a Developer Portfolio Project Showcase
description: A bootcamp graduate wants a project showcase where each project has a live demo, code link, tech stack, and a short story.
task: Design the layout and interaction of a developer portfolio project section. How would you present projects to impress hiring managers while remaining scannable?
hint: Think about visual hierarchy — image/demo first, title and tech stack second, story on hover/click. Use a grid layout with featured projects larger.
approach: Layout: 2-column grid with one featured project spanning full width at top. Each project card: screenshot thumbnail with hover animation showing live demo button, title, 2-3 sentence problem statement, tech stack pills (React, Node, PostgreSQL etc), GitHub and live demo links. Filter by technology using tag pills at top. Featured project gets a full-width card with screenshot on left, story on right. Show '3 things I learned' for each project to demonstrate growth. Add a skills matrix visualization showing proficiency in each tech.

title: Build a Daily Journaling App
description: A person wants a private digital journal that prompts them with daily questions and tracks mood over time.
task: Design a journaling app with daily prompts, mood tracking, and a timeline view. How would you keep the writing experience distraction-free?
hint: Use a full-screen writing mode with the prompt at the top. Store entries encrypted in localStorage for privacy.
approach: Daily prompt pool of 100+ questions (randomized daily). Full-screen writing mode: white background, centered text, no UI distractions. Mood selector: 5 emoji options at top. Entry is auto-saved every 30 seconds. Timeline view: calendar with mood color per day, click to re-read entries. Mood trend chart over 30/90 days. Streak counter and writing time tracked. Encrypt entries in localStorage using a user-set password (AES via CryptoJS). Weekly email digest (opt-in) with mood summary and a memory from a year ago.

title: Create a Collaborative Voting App
description: A team needs a real-time app for planning poker — where developers vote on story complexity without being influenced by others.
task: Design a planning poker app where team members submit votes simultaneously and results are only revealed after everyone votes. How would you handle real-time sync and reveal?
hint: Use WebSockets to broadcast vote states. Keep votes hidden server-side until all players have voted, then reveal all at once.
approach: Session: host creates room with a code, others join. Story input at top. Vote cards: Fibonacci sequence (1,2,3,5,8,13,21, ?, ∞). Each player selects their vote (hidden from others until reveal). Server tracks: {playerId, hasVoted, vote}. Display: each player as a card face-down. When all have voted, host clicks 'Reveal' — all cards flip simultaneously. Show: average, median, distribution histogram. Flag high disagreement (std dev > 3) for discussion. Replay previous stories in the session. Export estimates to CSV.

title: Design an Accessibility Checker
description: A developer wants a browser tool that checks their web pages for common accessibility violations and suggests fixes.
task: Design an accessibility auditing tool that checks for WCAG violations. Which checks would you prioritize? How would you present results to developers?
hint: Use the axe-core library for programmatic accessibility testing. Categorize issues by WCAG level (A, AA, AAA) and by impact (critical, serious, moderate).
approach: Checks to implement: missing alt text on images, form labels not associated with inputs, insufficient color contrast (WCAG 4.5:1 ratio), missing ARIA roles, keyboard focus not visible, links with ambiguous text ('click here'), heading hierarchy skipped. Use axe-core library for automated detection. Results panel: grouped by impact level, each issue shows: affected element highlighted in page, description of the problem, code snippet, how-to-fix guidance. Show pass/fail score out of 100. Export accessibility report as PDF. Watch mode to re-check on DOM changes.

title: Build a QR Code Generator and Scanner
description: A restaurant wants to generate QR codes for their menu and let customers scan them to view the digital menu.
task: Design a QR code generator and scanner web app. How would you generate styled QR codes and use the device camera to scan them in the browser?
hint: Use qrcode.js for generation and ZXing-js for scanning. Access the camera via getUserMedia() API.
approach: Generator: input field for URL/text, use qrcode.js to render QR on a canvas. Styling options: dot style, corner style, foreground/background color, center logo upload. Download as PNG or SVG. Scanner: access camera via navigator.mediaDevices.getUserMedia, draw video frames to canvas, run ZXing-js frame-by-frame to detect QR code. Success: beep sound + vibration + show decoded text. History of scanned/generated codes in localStorage. Batch generator for multiple QR codes from a CSV of URLs.

title: Design a GitHub Activity Visualizer
description: A developer wants a beautiful visualization of their GitHub activity beyond the default contribution graph.
task: Design a GitHub activity dashboard using the GitHub API. What visualizations would you create beyond the contribution graph? How would you handle API rate limiting?
hint: GitHub API returns commits, PRs, issues, and starred repos. Cache responses aggressively since data doesn't change by the minute.
approach: Fetch via GitHub GraphQL API for efficiency. Visualizations: (1) Language breakdown donut chart across all repos, (2) Contribution heatmap with custom colors, (3) PR merge time histogram, (4) Commit time-of-day radar chart (when does this dev code?), (5) Streak statistics, (6) Top repos by stars and activity. Cache all API responses in localStorage with a 1-hour TTL. Handle rate limiting: show remaining requests, offer OAuth login for 5000/hr limit. Progressive loading — show cached data instantly while fetching fresh.

title: Build a Text Summarizer Tool
description: A student wants to paste long articles and get concise bullet-point summaries with key takeaways.
task: Design an AI text summarizer. How would you handle very long texts that exceed LLM context limits? How would you let users customize summary length and format?
hint: For long texts, use a map-reduce approach: summarize chunks individually, then summarize the summaries.
approach: UI: large textarea for input, options panel (summary length: brief/medium/detailed, format: bullets/paragraph/executive, focus: key points/action items/questions raised). For texts under 4000 tokens: single LLM call. For longer texts: split into chunks of 2000 tokens with 200-token overlap, summarize each chunk, then combine summaries with a final LLM call. Show: original word count, summary word count, compression ratio. Copy to clipboard button. Save summaries to a local history. Add a 'generate quiz questions' mode from the summary.

title: Create a Time Zone Converter Dashboard
description: A remote team spread across 8 time zones struggles to find meeting times that work for everyone.
task: Design a time zone dashboard for remote teams. How would you show everyone's current time, working hours, and find overlap windows for meetings?
hint: Use the Intl.DateTimeFormat API for timezone conversion. Color-code working hours (green) vs off hours (red) for quick visual scanning.
approach: Add team members with their timezone and working hours (default 9-5). Show a grid: rows = team members, columns = every hour of the day. Color cells: green (everyone working), yellow (partial overlap), red (outside hours). Current time highlighted for each person with a moving cursor. Meeting time picker: select duration, system highlights best windows. 24-hour scrollable timeline view. Auto-detect user's timezone on first load. Share team configuration via URL params. Show how many hours of overlap exist between any two people.

title: Design a Video Timestamp Note-Taker
description: A student watching online lectures wants to take timestamped notes that link to exact moments in the video.
task: Build a tool that syncs notes with video timestamps. How would you let users click a timestamp in their notes to jump to that moment in the video?
hint: Use the YouTube iframe API to control video playback programmatically. Insert timestamps automatically when the user starts typing a note.
approach: Split layout: video player left, notes editor right. When user clicks in notes area, auto-insert current timestamp [MM:SS]. Parsing: on note display, render timestamps as clickable buttons that call player.seekTo(seconds). YouTube embed uses iframe API. Support pasting YouTube URLs to load video. Keyboard shortcut (Cmd+T) to insert timestamp while watching. Export notes as PDF with timestamps, or Markdown. Side panel showing all timestamps as a clickable table of contents. Auto-save notes to localStorage keyed by video ID.

title: Build a Custom Form Builder
description: A non-technical user wants to create custom forms with various field types and receive submissions by email.
task: Design a drag-and-drop form builder with field types (text, email, dropdown, checkbox, date), validation rules, and form embed functionality.
hint: Store form schema as a JSON array of field definitions. Render the form from the schema. Use formData API to collect and submit values.
approach: Field types: text, textarea, email, number, phone, date, dropdown, checkbox group, radio, file upload. Builder: drag field types from a panel onto the form. Each field has: label, placeholder, required toggle, validation rules (min/max length, regex pattern). Form schema stored as JSON. Preview mode shows live form. On submission: validate all fields client-side, POST to serverless function (Vercel/Netlify), send email via SendGrid. Embed via iframe or script tag. Dashboard shows all submissions with CSV export. Add conditional logic (show field B only if field A equals X).

title: Create a Developer Documentation Site Generator
description: An open source library needs beautiful documentation generated from markdown files and code comments.
task: Design a documentation site generator that takes markdown files and generates a searchable, navigable docs site. How would you handle versioning and search?
hint: Use a file system watcher during development and a build step for production. Generate a search index at build time using lunr.js.
approach: Input: folder of .md files with front matter (title, order, category). Build step: parse all markdown, generate HTML pages, build lunr.js search index from all content. Navigation: auto-generate from folder structure and front matter order. Code blocks: syntax highlight with Prism, add copy button. Versioning: separate folders per version, version switcher in header. Search: real-time client-side search using the pre-built lunr index — show results with context snippets. Dark mode. Edit on GitHub button per page. Table of contents auto-generated from headings.

title: Design a Password Manager
description: A user wants a secure local password manager that never sends passwords to a server.
task: Design a fully local password manager with strong encryption. How would you encrypt passwords? How would you handle master password verification without storing it?
hint: Derive an encryption key from the master password using PBKDF2. Never store the master password — store only a verification hash.
approach: Master password → PBKDF2 with 100,000 iterations + salt → 256-bit AES key. All vault data encrypted with this key using AES-GCM. Verification: store a known test string encrypted with the key — if decryption succeeds, password is correct. Storage: encrypted blob in IndexedDB. Features: add/edit/delete entries (site, username, password, notes), generate strong passwords (length, symbols, no-ambiguous chars), search by site name, copy to clipboard with 30s auto-clear, auto-lock after 5min idle. Export encrypted backup file. Never make network requests.

title: Build a Stock Portfolio Tracker
description: An investor wants to track their portfolio performance, see gain/loss by position, and compare against the S&P 500.
task: Design a stock portfolio tracker with real-time price updates, P&L calculations, and benchmark comparison. How would you handle API rate limits for real-time prices?
hint: Use a free stock API like Alpha Vantage or Polygon.io. Cache prices with a 5-minute TTL to stay within rate limits.
approach: Holdings: {ticker, shares, avgCostBasis, purchaseDate}. Fetch current prices via API (cache 5min). Calculate: total value, gain/loss ($), gain/loss (%), day change. Allocation donut chart by position. Performance chart: portfolio vs S&P 500 over selected time range. Fetch historical prices for chart. Sector breakdown (fetch from company info API). Dividend tracker. Tax lot tracking (FIFO/LIFO). Paper portfolio mode — track without real money. Alert when position is up/down by X%. Mobile-first responsive design.

title: Create a Random Team Generator
description: A teacher wants to randomly assign 30 students to balanced teams for group projects, with specific constraints.
task: Design a team generator that creates balanced groups from a list of people with optional constraints (skills, gender balance, no same-school pairs). How would you solve the constraint satisfaction problem?
hint: Use a shuffling algorithm with constraint checking and backtracking. If constraints can't be met, show which constraints are conflicting.
approach: Input: list of people with optional tags (skill level, group, constraint). Settings: team size or number of teams. Algorithm: shuffle people, assign round-robin to teams, then check constraints. If violated: swap members between teams to fix violations. Repeat until all constraints satisfied or max iterations reached. Display: team cards with member names, drag-to-swap between teams for manual adjustments. Export teams to CSV or Slack message format. Shuffle history so you can go back. 'Lock' specific people to specific teams before generating.

title: Design a Commit Message Generator
description: A developer wants an AI tool that generates conventional commit messages from a git diff.
task: Build an AI tool that reads a git diff and generates a proper conventional commit message. How would you handle large diffs? How would you format the output?
hint: Parse the diff to extract changed files and lines. Send a summarized diff to an LLM with a specific conventional commits prompt.
approach: CLI tool: run in git repo, get diff via `git diff --staged`. If diff > 4000 tokens: summarize each file's changes separately first. LLM prompt: 'Given this git diff, write a conventional commit message following the format: type(scope): subject. Types: feat, fix, docs, style, refactor, test, chore. Be specific and concise.' Show 3 alternative commit messages. Let user select or edit. Auto-copy to clipboard. VS Code extension: show suggestions in the commit input. Learn from user's past commits to match their style.

title: Build an Invoice Generator
description: A freelancer needs a professional invoice generator that exports to PDF without any subscription fees.
task: Design a free, browser-based invoice generator. How would you render a professional-looking invoice and export it as PDF without a backend?
hint: Use window.print() with a print-specific CSS to convert the invoice HTML to PDF. Or use jsPDF library for programmatic PDF generation.
approach: Form inputs: your company info (saved in localStorage), client info, line items (description, qty, rate), tax rate, payment terms, notes. Calculate: subtotals, tax, total. Invoice preview updates live as you type. PDF export: use jsPDF + html2canvas to capture the rendered invoice. Invoice number auto-increments. Support multiple currencies. Save invoice history locally. Send via email using mailto: link. Recurring invoice templates. Professional designs to choose from (modern, classic, minimal). Add your logo via image upload.

title: Create a Regex Builder and Tester
description: A developer struggles with complex regex patterns and wants a visual tool to build and test them interactively.
task: Design an interactive regex builder that highlights matches in real-time, explains the pattern in plain English, and shows common pattern templates.
hint: Use an LLM to explain regex patterns in plain English. Highlight matches using the replace() method with capture groups.
approach: Two panels: regex input at top, test string below. Highlight: run regex on test string, wrap matches in <mark> tags with different colors for different capture groups. Explanation: send regex to LLM, ask it to explain each part in plain English (e.g. \d+ means 'one or more digits'). Pattern library: common patterns (email, URL, phone, date, IP address, hex color). Show: match count, all match results in a table with groups. Flags toggle (g, i, m, s). Replace mode: test regex replace with a replacement string. Copy pattern with/without delimiters.

title: Design a Code Interview Practice Platform
description: A developer preparing for technical interviews wants practice problems with hints, solutions, and time tracking.
task: Design a coding interview practice platform. How would you run code securely in the browser? How would you provide hints without spoiling the solution?
hint: Use Pyodide for Python execution in the browser (WebAssembly), or Judge0 API for multi-language execution with sandboxing.
approach: Problem set: categorized (arrays, trees, DP, graphs) with difficulty tags. Code editor: Monaco (VS Code's editor) with language selection. Code execution: Judge0 API for secure sandboxed execution. Test cases: run all tests, show pass/fail with input/output. Hints system: tiered (1. conceptual approach, 2. algorithm hint, 3. pseudocode, 4. solution) — unlocking costs 'hint points'. Timer visible during practice. After solving: show time/space complexity analysis, alternative solutions, discussion section. Track personal solve history and time-to-solve trends.

title: Build a Daily Standup Summarizer
description: A team lead wants an AI tool that collects daily standup updates from team members and creates a concise summary.
task: Design a standup summarizer that collects responses to 'what did you do, what will you do, any blockers' and generates a team summary. How would you handle async input from different time zones?
hint: Allow async submission by each team member. Close the collection window after a set time, then generate the summary.
approach: Each team member submits standup asynchronously (web form or Slack slash command). Deadline: 10am manager's timezone. After deadline: LLM prompt sends all submissions and asks to: (1) group updates by theme/project, (2) highlight blockers prominently, (3) identify common threads across team, (4) flag if anyone is blocked by someone else. Output: formatted Slack message and email. Track attendance (who submitted vs. who didn't). Show streaks. Over time: identify recurring blockers as systemic issues. Weekly summary of progress themes.

title: Create a Mind Map Builder
description: A writer wants a visual mind mapping tool to brainstorm ideas and connections before writing articles.
task: Design a browser-based mind map builder with drag nodes, connecting edges, and keyboard navigation. How would you layout nodes automatically?
hint: Use an SVG canvas for drawing. Implement a radial tree layout algorithm for automatic organization. Store the graph as an adjacency list.
approach: Data structure: {nodes: [{id, text, x, y, color}], edges: [{from, to}]}. Rendering: SVG for connections (quadratic bezier curves), HTML divs for nodes (for text editing). Add node: double-click canvas → new node at cursor. Connect: drag from node edge → draw temporary line → drop on target. Auto-layout: radial tree from root, D3 hierarchy layout algorithm. Edit: double-click node to edit inline text. Collapse subtrees. Color coding per branch. Keyboard: Tab to create child, Enter to create sibling, Delete to remove. Export as PNG, SVG, or JSON. Undo/redo stack.

title: Design an API Playground
description: A frontend developer wants a lightweight alternative to Postman that runs entirely in the browser.
task: Build a browser-based API client. How would you handle CORS for API calls? How would you store request history and collections?
hint: CORS prevents direct browser-to-API calls. Offer a proxy option (self-hosted or cloud function) to forward requests server-side.
approach: Request builder: URL, method, headers (key-value editor), body (JSON with formatting/validation, form-data). Response viewer: formatted JSON with collapsible tree, response headers, status code with color coding, time and size. History: last 50 requests in localStorage. Collections: group related requests, import/export as JSON. Environment variables: {{baseUrl}} substitution in URLs and headers. CORS: offer CORS proxy toggle for local development. Pre-request scripts: run JS to set headers dynamically (auth tokens). Share requests via URL-encoded state. GraphQL mode with schema explorer.

title: Build a Screen Recording Transcriber
description: A remote worker wants to record a meeting and get an automatic transcript with speaker labels.
task: Design a system that records audio, transcribes it with speaker diarization, and produces a searchable transcript. How would you identify different speakers?
hint: Use the MediaRecorder API for recording. Send audio to Whisper API for transcription and AssemblyAI or AWS Transcribe for speaker diarization.
approach: Recording: MediaRecorder API captures audio. Upload to S3 or directly to transcription API. Transcription + diarization: AssemblyAI (supports speaker labels). Poll for completion. Display: scrollable transcript with Speaker 1/2/3 labels and timestamps. Speaker identification: let user label Speaker 1 = 'Alice', etc. Search: highlight search terms in transcript, jump to timestamps. Export: plain text, SRT subtitles, Word document. Summary: send transcript to LLM to extract action items and decisions. Integration: share transcript link with team.

title: Create a Learning Path Generator
description: A self-learner wants a personalized curriculum for learning a new skill, organized as a week-by-week plan.
task: Design an AI-powered learning path generator that creates a personalized curriculum based on the user's goal, current level, and available weekly hours. How would you structure the output?
hint: Prompt the LLM to generate a structured JSON curriculum with weeks, topics, resources, and exercises. Then render it as a beautiful interactive roadmap.
approach: Input form: goal (e.g., 'Learn React'), current level (beginner/intermediate/advanced), hours per week, preferred learning style (videos/reading/projects), target date. LLM prompt generates JSON: {weeks: [{weekNumber, topic, objectives[], resources:[{title, url, type, duration}], project, quiz}]}. Render as timeline roadmap. Users can check off completed items. Progress bar per week and overall. Adjust pace: if falling behind, regenerate from current week. Resource types: video (YouTube), reading (blog/docs), practice (LeetCode, exercises). Add to calendar integration.

title: Design a CSS Animation Studio
description: A frontend developer wants a visual tool to create and preview CSS animations without writing keyframes by hand.
task: Design an interactive CSS animation builder. How would you represent animation keyframes visually? How would you generate the final CSS output?
hint: Represent the animation timeline as a horizontal bar with keyframe markers. Each marker corresponds to a percentage (0%, 50%, 100%) with its CSS properties.
approach: Canvas: show the animated element (user chooses shape/text/image). Timeline: horizontal bar at bottom, drag markers for keyframes (0%, 25%, 50%, 75%, 100%). Per-keyframe properties: transform (translate, rotate, scale, skew), opacity, background-color, border-radius. Use CSS custom properties to update preview in real time. Easing: visual cubic-bezier editor. Presets: bounce, pulse, shake, float, fade. Generate clean CSS output: copy to clipboard. Export as React component or vanilla CSS class. Preview controls: play, pause, loop, speed. Multiple animation layers.

title: Build a Real Estate Listing Aggregator
description: A home buyer wants to compare properties across multiple listing sites without opening 10 browser tabs.
task: Design a property comparison tool. How would you normalize data from different sources? How would you display a side-by-side property comparison?
hint: Use a browser extension to extract listing data from pages the user visits, storing it locally for comparison.
approach: Browser extension: detect when user is on a property listing page (Zillow, Realtor, etc), extract structured data (price, sqft, beds/baths, address, photos, description) using site-specific selectors. Store in extension storage. Comparison dashboard: grid layout with each property as a column. Highlighted differences in red/green. Map view showing all properties with markers. Calculate derived metrics: price per sqft, estimated monthly mortgage, commute time to user's workplace (Google Maps API). Save/unsave properties. Share comparison as a URL-encoded link. Add user notes per property.

title: Create a Resume Parser and Analyzer
description: An HR tool needs to parse resumes uploaded as PDFs and extract structured information automatically.
task: Design a resume parser that extracts name, contact info, skills, experience, and education from uploaded PDFs. How would you handle varied resume formats?
hint: Use pdf.js to extract text from PDFs, then send the raw text to an LLM with a structured extraction prompt.
approach: Upload PDF → pdf.js extracts raw text. Send text to LLM with prompt: 'Extract the following from this resume as JSON: {name, email, phone, linkedIn, skills[], experience:[{company, title, startDate, endDate, bullets[]}], education:[{school, degree, year}]}. Return only valid JSON.' Parse and validate the JSON response. Display: structured profile card with all fields. Skill tag cloud. Experience timeline. Score the resume for a given job description (similarity matching). ATS keyword analysis: what keywords are missing from a job description. Export back to formatted PDF.

title: Build a Cursor Trail and Particle Effect Library
description: A creative web developer wants to add fun cursor effects to their portfolio — trails, sparks, and particle bursts on click.
task: Design a lightweight cursor effects library. How would you render particles efficiently without causing performance issues? How would you keep it under 5KB?
hint: Use a single canvas overlay for all particles. Use requestAnimationFrame with a particle pool to avoid garbage collection pauses.
approach: Single full-screen canvas positioned fixed above all content. Particle pool: pre-allocate 200 particles, reuse them instead of creating/destroying (reduces GC). On mousemove: spawn a trail particle at cursor position. On click: burst 20 particles in random directions with random colors. Each particle: {x, y, vx, vy, alpha, size, color, life}. Update loop: each frame, update position, reduce alpha, reduce size. Remove when alpha <= 0 (return to pool). Effects: trail (tiny dots that fade), sparkle (star shapes), text (emojis explode on click). No dependencies. CSS pointer-events: none on canvas so it doesn't interfere with UI.

title: Design a Local-First Database App
description: A developer wants a notes and tasks app that stores data locally using IndexedDB and optionally syncs to the cloud.
task: Design a local-first app with IndexedDB as the primary store. How would you structure the database? How would you implement optional cloud sync?
hint: Use Dexie.js as an IndexedDB wrapper. For sync, use a CRDT (like Automerge or Yjs) to resolve conflicts between local and remote state.
approach: Dexie.js schema: notes table (id, title, body, tags[], createdAt, updatedAt, syncStatus). All writes go to IndexedDB first — instant response. Sync (optional): user provides their own storage (Dropbox, S3, or self-hosted). On online event: compare local updatedAt with remote. Conflicts: show diff and let user choose, or use CRDT auto-merge. Offline-first UI: never show 'loading' for local data. Sync indicator in corner. Full-text search with Fuse.js over all notes. Version history: keep last 10 versions of each note. Export as zip of markdown files.

title: Create a Browser-Based Photo Editor
description: A blogger wants basic photo editing (crop, filter, resize, brightness) without installing Photoshop.
task: Design a browser-based image editor. How would you apply filters in real-time without performance issues? How would you implement non-destructive editing?
hint: Use Canvas 2D API for basic operations. For GPU-accelerated filters, use WebGL or CSS filters for preview with Canvas for final export.
approach: Non-destructive: keep original image in memory, apply edits as a pipeline on each render. Adjustments: brightness (scale pixel values), contrast (redistribute), saturation (modify HSL), warmth (shift color channels), vignette (radial gradient overlay). Filters: B&W, vintage, cool, warm (preset adjustment combinations). Crop: overlay with drag handles. Resize: canvas rescale. Blur: convolution matrix. Undo/redo: store edit history as a list of operations, replay from original. Preview via CSS filters for speed, final export re-renders on canvas. Download as PNG/JPEG with quality slider. Use Web Workers for heavy operations to keep UI responsive.

title: Design a Smart Notification System
description: An app sends too many notifications and users are ignoring them. The team wants intelligent batching and prioritization.
task: Design a smart notification system that batches low-priority alerts, respects user quiet hours, and learns from dismissal patterns. How would you prioritize and deliver notifications?
hint: Assign a priority score to each notification based on urgency, user's historical engagement, and time of day. Only send immediately for high-priority items.
approach: Notification model: {id, type, priority, content, userId, createdAt}. Priority scoring: base priority (P1-P4) * recency factor * user-engagement coefficient (higher if user usually engages with this type). Quiet hours: user sets 10pm-8am, hold all non-P1 notifications. Batching: collect P3/P4 notifications for 4 hours, send digest. Delivery: Web Push for background, in-app toast for active users. Learning: track open/dismiss/snooze per notification type. After 100 interactions, adjust priority scores per type per user. Weekly digest option for lowest priority. Preference center: granular on/off per notification type.

title: Build a Competitive Programming Timer
description: A competitive programmer wants a tool to simulate contest conditions — countdown timer, problem set display, and submission tracking.
task: Design a competitive programming session simulator with a countdown timer, problem list, solve tracking, and penalty calculation (like ICPC rules).
hint: ICPC scoring: teams ranked by problems solved, then by total time + 20min penalty per wrong attempt.
approach: Setup: duration (e.g., 3 hours), number of problems. Timer: large countdown, turns red in final 10 minutes. Problem panel: A-J letters with status (unsolved, attempting, solved). Log attempts: for each problem, track submission time and correct/wrong. Calculate score: count solved + time score (minutes since start + 20min per WA). Rank display if multiple users (team mode). Sounds: tick in final minute, bell on solve. At contest end: scoreboard summary, problems solved/attempted stats. Practice mode: random problem from Codeforces API. Export contest log.

title: Create a Multi-Language Code Translator
description: A Python developer wants to convert their scripts to JavaScript without rewriting them from scratch.
task: Build an AI code translator that converts code between programming languages. How would you handle idioms and library differences that don't have direct equivalents?
hint: Use an LLM with a prompt that explicitly asks it to translate idioms, not just syntax, and to note where no direct equivalent exists.
approach: UI: two code editors side-by-side (Monaco). Source language selector + target language selector. Translate button sends source code to LLM with prompt: 'Translate this [source] code to [target]. Preserve the logic exactly. For each library or idiom with no direct equivalent, add a comment explaining the translation choice. Use idiomatic [target] style, not a direct word-for-word translation.' Highlight translated lines corresponding to source lines. Show warnings for known problem areas (e.g., Python's list comprehensions to JS). Copy/download translated code. History of translations.

title: Design a Browser History Analyzer
description: A curious user wants to analyze their own browsing patterns — most visited sites, peak hours, and category breakdown.
task: Design a browser extension that analyzes the user's browsing history locally and shows privacy-safe statistics. How would you categorize sites without sending data to a server?
hint: Use the history API provided by browser extensions. Categorize sites client-side using a local domain-to-category mapping file.
approach: Extension with history permission. Read history via chrome.history.search. Process: group by domain, count visits, count time spent (if available). Categorize: match domains against a bundled dictionary (google.com → Search, github.com → Development, netflix.com → Entertainment). Privacy: all processing in browser, nothing sent externally. Visualizations: top 20 domains bar chart, category donut chart, visits-by-hour heatmap, daily activity timeline. Block-site feature: add a site to focus list and block it during focus hours. Export anonymized stats as CSV.

title: Build a Customizable Dashboard
description: A power user wants a personal homepage with draggable widgets showing weather, news, tasks, and bookmarks.
task: Design a customizable dashboard with draggable, resizable widgets. How would you persist layouts? How would you build a widget plugin system?
hint: Use CSS Grid with react-grid-layout for drag and resize. Store layout as JSON in localStorage. Each widget is a self-contained component.
approach: Layout engine: react-grid-layout stores positions as [{i, x, y, w, h}] grid units. Widgets: Clock, Weather (openweathermap), Top News (newsapi), Todo List, Bookmarks, GitHub Contributions, Spotify Now Playing, Quote of the Day, Countdown Timer. Each widget is a standalone React component with its own config modal. Widget catalog: click + to add widgets from a gallery. Themes: color schemes + background (solid, gradient, unsplash photo). Settings: 12/24h, temperature units, news categories. Export/import dashboard config as JSON. Mobile responsive.

title: Create an Interactive Data Story
description: A journalist wants to present data in a scroll-driven narrative format where charts update as the reader scrolls.
task: Design a scrollytelling framework for data journalism. How would you tie chart animations to scroll position? How would you make it mobile-friendly?
hint: Use Intersection Observer to detect when narrative paragraphs enter the viewport, and animate the chart accordingly.
approach: Layout: sticky chart panel on the right, scrollable text paragraphs on the left. Each paragraph has a data-state attribute linking to a chart state. Intersection Observer: when paragraph enters viewport, trigger chart transition to corresponding state. D3.js for animated charts — smooth transitions between states using d3.transition(). Chart types: bar race (ranking over time), choropleth map (geographic data), scatter plot (two variables over time). Mobile: chart on top, text below, use full-width layout. Fallback: static screenshots for no-JS environments. Export as PNG at each state.

title: Design a Terminal Emulator in the Browser
description: A web developer wants to embed an interactive terminal in their documentation site for running code examples.
task: Design an in-browser terminal that can run simple shell commands or Python scripts. How would you handle the execution environment and security?
hint: Use xterm.js for the terminal UI. For Python execution, use Pyodide (WebAssembly). For shell commands, implement a limited command interpreter in JS.
approach: xterm.js for terminal rendering (handles colors, cursor, history). Input handling: capture keystrokes, echo to terminal, build command string, execute on Enter. Command interpreter: implement subset of bash (cd, ls, cat, echo, mkdir, python). File system: virtual in-memory FS using BrowserFS. Python execution: load Pyodide (Python in WebAssembly) lazily. For docs use: pre-configure a tutorial environment (files already present). Security: everything runs client-side in WebAssembly sandbox — no network access, no real file system. Tab completion. Command history (up arrow). Session persistence in sessionStorage.

title: Build a Social Media Content Calendar
description: A content creator wants to plan, write, and schedule posts for multiple social platforms in one place.
task: Design a content calendar for managing social media posts across platforms. How would you visualize the calendar? How would AI help with content generation?
hint: A weekly grid view with platform icons per slot is more useful than a traditional calendar. Add AI writing assistance per post.
approach: Calendar views: month (overview), week (planning), day (detail). Post card: platform icon (Twitter/IG/LinkedIn), text preview, scheduled time, status (draft/scheduled/published). Create post: rich text editor with character counter per platform, image upload, hashtag suggestions. AI assist: 'Write a post about [topic] in the style of [brand voice]' — generates 3 options. Optimal time suggestions: based on platform best practices. Content categories: color-code by content type (educational, promotional, engagement). Analytics: track which content types get most engagement. CSV import of post schedule.

title: Create a Dependency Graph Visualizer
description: A developer wants to visualize the module dependency graph of their JavaScript project to identify circular dependencies.
task: Design a tool that visualizes JavaScript module dependencies as an interactive graph. How would you parse imports? How would you highlight circular dependencies?
hint: Use @babel/parser to parse JS files and extract import statements. Use D3 force-directed graph for visualization.
approach: CLI: scan all .js/.ts files in a project, use @babel/parser to extract import/export statements. Build adjacency list: {module: [imports[]]}. Detect cycles: DFS with in-progress set (like directed graph cycle detection). Visualization: D3 force-directed graph. Nodes: modules (sized by number of imports). Edges: directed arrows. Circular deps: highlighted in red with animation. Click node: highlight only its direct dependencies. Filter: show only local modules (exclude node_modules). Cluster: group by folder. Export as SVG or JSON. Stats: most imported module, most circular deps, avg dependency depth.

title: Design a Multiplayer Quiz Game
description: A teacher wants a live quiz game where students join with a code and compete in real-time like Kahoot.
task: Design a real-time multiplayer quiz platform. How would you sync question display and answer collection across all players simultaneously? How would you calculate scores?
hint: Use WebSockets to synchronize game state. The host controls the game flow; all clients display the same question simultaneously.
approach: Host creates quiz, gets a 6-character room code. Players join via code, enter nickname. Game states: lobby → question → reveal → leaderboard → (next question) → final. Sync via WebSocket broadcast. Question display: host clicks 'Start' → server broadcasts question to all clients simultaneously. 30-second timer shown on all screens. On answer: player submits, server records time. After timer: reveal correct answer, animate scores. Score = correctness * speed bonus. Leaderboard updates after each question. Final screen: winner podium + full rankings. Export results. Quiz creator with image questions.

title: Build a Text-to-Diagram Converter
description: A developer wants to describe a system architecture in plain English and get a diagram automatically generated.
task: Design a tool that converts natural language descriptions into architecture/flow diagrams. How would you bridge LLM text output to a visual diagram?
hint: Ask the LLM to generate Mermaid.js syntax from the description. Mermaid renders many diagram types from text definitions.
approach: Input: user describes system in plain English ('User sends request to load balancer, which routes to one of 3 app servers, they query PostgreSQL database cached by Redis'). LLM prompt: 'Convert this to Mermaid.js diagram syntax. Use appropriate diagram type (flowchart, sequence, ER, etc).' Render with Mermaid.js in the browser. Show both: rendered diagram and the Mermaid source code. Let user edit the Mermaid code directly and see live preview. Diagram types to support: flowchart, sequence diagram, class diagram, ER diagram, Gantt. Export as SVG or PNG. Save diagrams to a gallery.

title: Create a Browser-Based E-Commerce Store
description: A crafter wants to sell 20 handmade products online without paying for Shopify — everything runs in the browser with Stripe.
task: Design a minimal e-commerce site using only static hosting. How would you handle cart state, checkout, and Stripe payment without a backend?
hint: Use Stripe's Payment Links or Checkout Sessions. Products can be defined in a JSON file. Use localStorage for cart state.
approach: Products JSON file: [{id, name, description, price, images[], stock}]. Cart: managed in localStorage. Product listing: grid of cards with image, name, price, add-to-cart button. Cart sidebar: running total, quantity controls. Checkout: use Stripe Payment Links (pre-created per product) or redirect to Stripe Checkout via a serverless function (Vercel). Order confirmation: use Stripe webhook → serverless function → send email via SendGrid. Admin: separate password-protected page to update product JSON. No backend required for catalog — just a static site on Vercel/Netlify + one serverless function for Stripe.

title: Design a Debate Practice Assistant
description: A student wants an AI debate partner that argues the opposite side of any topic to sharpen their argumentation skills.
task: Design an AI debate training tool. How would you prompt the AI to consistently argue one side? How would you evaluate the quality of the user's arguments?
hint: Use system prompt to lock the AI into a specific stance. Use a separate LLM call to evaluate the user's argument quality.
approach: Setup: user enters topic and chooses their position. AI is system-prompted to argue the opposing side with conviction. UI: chat interface with rounds. After each user argument, AI responds with strongest counterargument + asks a probing question. After 3-5 rounds, separate evaluator LLM call assesses user's arguments: logical fallacies found, strongest points made, points missed, overall persuasiveness score (1-10). Debate modes: Oxford style, freestyle, Socratic questioning. Save debates as transcripts. Difficulty levels (AI argues harder or easier). Topic suggestions by category (politics, science, ethics).

title: Build a Gantt Chart Maker
description: A project manager wants a simple drag-and-drop Gantt chart tool without expensive project management software.
task: Design a browser-based Gantt chart builder. How would you implement drag-to-resize task bars? How would you handle task dependencies?
hint: Render the chart on an SVG or Canvas. Task bars are rectangles that respond to mousedown+mousemove for dragging and resizing.
approach: Data: {tasks:[{id, name, start, end, dependencies[], assignee, color}]}. Render: left panel is task list, right is timeline SVG. Timeline headers: months → weeks → days (zoom levels). Task bars: positioned by date-to-pixel mapping. Drag bar: moves task (update start/end). Drag right edge: resize (update end). Dependency arrows: draw lines between related tasks. Critical path: highlight the longest dependency chain. Zoom: scroll wheel changes time scale. Today marker: vertical red line. Milestones: diamond shape. Export as PNG. Import from CSV. Print-friendly export.

title: Create a Personal Recommendation Engine
description: A reader wants an AI that learns their taste in books, movies, and music and makes personalized recommendations.
task: Design a taste profile system that builds recommendations from user ratings. How would you represent taste as a vector? How would you use an LLM to explain recommendations?
hint: Collect explicit ratings (1-5 stars). Use a collaborative filtering approach or embed liked items and find similar ones semantically.
approach: Onboarding: rate 20 popular items across categories (books/movies/music). Taste profile: embed descriptions of highly-rated items using a sentence transformer, average embeddings to create taste vector. Recommendation: search a catalog using cosine similarity against taste vector. LLM explanation: 'You liked [X, Y, Z]. This recommendation is similar because [reason].' Feedback loop: rate recommendations to refine taste. Cross-domain: if you like crime novels, maybe crime movies. Discovery mode: suggest something outside your comfort zone. Weekly 'New Release' matches based on your taste profile. Privacy: all stored locally.

title: Build a Countdown Timer Collection
description: An event organizer wants beautiful countdown timers for upcoming events, embedded on a webpage.
task: Design a countdown timer widget library with multiple themes (digital, analog, minimal, neon). How would you handle different time scales (seconds vs years away)?
hint: Use setInterval with 1-second ticks. Calculate remaining time as days, hours, minutes, seconds. Auto-detect appropriate granularity.
approach: Timer component: takes target date, theme, and label. Calculate: totalMs = targetDate - now → decompose to days/hours/minutes/seconds. For events far away (>30 days): show days prominently. For imminent events: show hours:minutes:seconds. Themes: Digital (LCD font, dark bg), Minimal (large numbers, thin font), Neon (glowing text, dark bg), Analog (clock face). Flip animation: numbers flip like an airport departure board. On completion: show celebration animation (confetti), play sound. Timezone support. Multiple timers on one page. Shareable URL with timer config encoded.

title: Design a Fake Data Generator
description: A backend developer needs realistic fake data (users, products, orders) for testing their API without real user data.
task: Design a fake data generation tool that creates realistic datasets in various formats. How would you make the fake data internally consistent (e.g., orders reference real users)?
hint: Use Faker.js for realistic values. Build entities in order: users first, then products, then orders referencing valid user and product IDs.
approach: Schema builder: define entity types and their fields with faker generators. E.g., User: {id: uuid, name: faker.name(), email: faker.email(), createdAt: date}. Relationships: Order.userId references a generated User.id. Generation: topological sort of entity types by dependencies, generate in order. Output formats: JSON, CSV, SQL INSERT statements, TypeScript types. Count control per entity (50 users, 200 orders). Preview: table view with 10 sample rows. Custom templates: define custom schemas with real column names. Export all as a zip. Locale support (Indian names, addresses, phone numbers).

title: Create a Daily Briefing Email Generator
description: An executive wants a daily automated email at 7am summarizing news, calendar, tasks, and weather.
task: Design an automated daily briefing system. How would you aggregate content from different sources? How would the AI synthesize it into a readable brief?
hint: Use a CRON job to trigger at 7am. Fetch from news API, calendar API, todo API, and weather API. Send everything to the LLM to write a cohesive brief.
approach: Data sources: Weather API (current + forecast), Google Calendar API (today's events), Todoist/Notion API (due tasks), News API (headlines filtered by saved topics), Stock API (portfolio summary). Aggregation CRON: 6:50am daily → fetch all → send to LLM with prompt: 'Write a professional morning briefing email. Lead with weather and key appointments. Then major news relevant to [topics]. End with 3 most important tasks for the day.' Email via SendGrid. HTML template with sections. User preferences: choose topics, portfolio tickers, calendar accounts. Gradual learning: if user often replies asking about a topic, add it automatically.

title: Build a Circuit Breaker Visualizer
description: A senior engineer wants to demonstrate circuit breaker patterns to junior developers through interactive visualization.
task: Design an interactive visualization of the circuit breaker pattern in distributed systems. How would you animate state transitions and make the concept intuitive?
hint: Show three states: CLOSED (normal), OPEN (failing), HALF-OPEN (testing). Animate requests flowing through and failing/succeeding.
approach: Visual: two services connected by a circuit breaker (visualized as an electrical switch). States: CLOSED (green, switch closed, requests flowing), OPEN (red, switch open, requests rejected immediately), HALF-OPEN (yellow, a test request allowed through). Animation: requests travel left-to-right as moving dots. Failed requests flash red. Controls: failure rate slider (0-100%), latency slider, threshold (how many failures to trip). Real-time: stats counter (success/fail/rejected). State machine diagram alongside showing current state. Code panel shows the pattern in code. 'Try it' button sends a burst of requests with current settings.

title: Create a Local Grocery Shopping Optimizer
description: A household manager wants to enter their shopping list and get items organized by grocery store aisle to minimize walking.
task: Design a shopping list app that organizes items by store section. How would you map items to aisles? How would you let users customize their store's layout?
hint: Use a predefined item-to-category mapping (milk → Dairy, apples → Produce). Let users drag aisles to reorder them to match their store.
approach: Item database: 500+ common items pre-mapped to categories (Produce, Dairy, Meat, Frozen, Bakery, Pantry, Snacks, Beverages, Household, Personal Care). Add item → auto-categorize → user can override. Aisle order: drag-and-drop list of sections in the user's store order (saved to localStorage). Shopping view: items grouped by section in aisle order with checkboxes. As items checked off: cross out or move to 'collected' section. Voice input: 'Add two pounds of chicken' using Web Speech API. Recurring list: remember weekly staples. Price estimate: rough totals if prices added. Share list via WhatsApp/iMessage.

title: Design a Code Diff Visualizer
description: A developer wants a beautiful code diff tool that highlights changes more intuitively than standard git diff output.
task: Design an interactive code diff viewer. How would you compute the diff algorithm? How would you make additions and deletions visually clear while preserving readability?
hint: Use the Myers diff algorithm or a library like diff for line-by-line and character-level diff computation.
approach: Compute: use jsdiff library for line diff, then character diff within changed lines. Display: side-by-side (old left, new right) or unified view. Added lines: green background. Removed lines: red background. Changed words within lines: darker green/red highlight. Collapsed sections: unchanged blocks collapsed with count (e.g., '42 lines unchanged'). Syntax highlighting: Prism.js detects language from filename or content. File header: filename, +N -M stats. Navigation: jump between changes with keyboard. Inline comments: click a line to add note. Export as image or HTML. Paste two code blocks or connect to GitHub PR.

title: Build a Random Challenge Generator
description: Developers at a hackathon want a tool that generates random project ideas combining a random domain, technology, and constraint.
task: Design an idea generator that combines random elements (domain, stack, constraint) into a feasible hackathon project brief. How would you ensure generated ideas are coherent?
hint: Instead of combining fully random elements, use themed sets — when domain is 'education', only pick education-appropriate technologies and constraints.
approach: Domain pool: Education, Healthcare, Environment, Finance, Gaming, Social, Productivity. Tech pool: React, Vue, Node.js, Python, ML, WebSocket, WebRTC, Maps API, AR. Constraint pool: Offline-first, Voice-only, Under 1MB, Accessible, 2-player, Real-time, No backend. Themed pairing: when domain=Healthcare, boost probability of ML, accessibility constraints. LLM enhancement: send the 3 random picks to an LLM and ask it to write a 3-sentence project brief that makes them coherently work together. Save liked ideas. Roll individual element to try different combos. Team size recommendation per complexity.

title: Create a Presentation Slide Timer
description: A conference speaker wants a tool that shows their slide-by-slide time allocations and alerts them if they're running behind.
task: Design a presentation timer that lets speakers plan time per slide and tracks their actual pace vs. planned. How would you show visual alerts without distracting the speaker?
hint: Show a subtle color shift (green → yellow → red) rather than alarming alerts. Show time-remaining and time-behind alongside the current slide timer.
approach: Setup: enter total presentation duration and number of slides (or time per slide individually). Per-slide target time automatically calculated or manually set. During presentation: large current slide timer, progress bar for overall presentation. Color indicator: green (on track), yellow (slightly behind), red (significantly behind). Keyboard shortcut (space/right arrow) to advance to next slide and log actual time spent. After presentation: actual vs. planned time per slide comparison chart. Identify which sections ran over. Export as report. Full-screen speaker notes view compatible.

title: Design a Music Theory Tutor
description: A beginner musician wants an interactive tool to learn music theory — scales, chords, intervals — with audio feedback.
task: Design a music theory learning app with an interactive piano keyboard and audio playback. How would you generate audio in the browser without pre-recorded samples?
